author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if preventable blindness isn’t a medical failure—but a systemic one? This is the story of 25 million Americans trapped in a healthcare gap, and the unexpected solution that's restoring sight to thousands.

After 40 years as an eye surgeon, Dr Levenson thought he'd seen everything. Then MrBeast—the internet's biggest creator—showed up at his Jacksonville clinic with a radical idea: cure 1,000 blind people, film it, and let the story pay for itself. What happened next reached 200 million people and proved something powerful: we don't have a blindness problem; we have a visibility problem.

This talk reveals:
Why working Americans are going blind despite a 15-minute cure
How a YouTube video became a proof-of-concept for community-based healthcare
The hidden economic gap that leaves 25 million Americans without access to basic eye surgery
Why storytelling—not policy—may be the fastest path to systemic change
How one local "Gift of Sight" program is scaling nationally through voluntee
title: I cured 1,000 blind people—then learned the real problem | Jeffrey Levenson | TEDxJacksonville

author: TEDx Talks
description: Professional athletes, musicians, and 15-year-olds all share one fear: the sophomore slump. High school English teacher Brianna Wheeler draws on three years of teaching sophomores to reveal why they are the most socially lonely and institutionally invisible group in school, and how understanding that invisibility, along with a powerful framework for categorizing knowledge, can help any of us navigate the disorienting experience of round two. Briana Wheeler teaches English at Webb School of Knoxville, where she serves as Chair of the Creative Writing Program and guides students through the creative process. A 2020 Sewanee graduate and Tennessee Williams Creative Writing Award winner, Briana continues to approach life through art, helping others discover the power of storytelling and creative expression. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: So you're a sophomore, what now? | Briana Wheeler | TEDxMurfreesboro

author: TEDx Talks
description: Joyce's story is one of "breaking and rebuilding". An unexpected wrist fracture caused the identity she had built on "perfection" and "victory" to crumble completely. Yet it was also in the ruins that she found more solid foundations: resilience, self-acceptance, and more. She came to realize that success is also about "how you fall, and how you stand back up". Hi everyone, I am Joyce, a nineth grader from RDF international School. For years, I’ve measured success by just plain numbers on academic scores. It’s all twirling around the “A”, the “100”, but I’ve never felt it until I broke my hand playing soccer just three months ago. Even though almost everyone around me advised me to stop sports, I went on with volleyball and soccer with an injured hand. The feeling I got isn’t the physical pain coming out of my bones, it’s success. Success is clinging to your passions and pursuing what you love even when it hurts. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but
title: Success  Redefine | Beyond the Finish Line and False Labels | Joyce Wang | TEDxRDFIS Youth

Beyond performing, he has also shaped the craft behind the curtain by directing, producing, and mentoring generations of performers.

Off stage, he brings that same depth into leadership and personal development. As a coach and consultant, he has worked across industries, helping individuals and organisations strengthen communication, emotional intelligence, and authentic leadership.

description: The story we tell about ourselves is often the hardest one to start. As a storytelling coach with nearly two decades of experience, Kara Kemp knows that the messy, imperfect, unfinished stories are the ones that build the deepest community. From a farm girl upbringing stitched with strong women's legacies to touring with music legends, to losing her mother and finding her baton, Kara traces how bold, brave spaces where people risk telling their truth become the most powerful agents of connection and change. Kara Kemp is a creative coach, storyteller, and touring-industry veteran who brings a whole-brain approach to leadership, creativity, and community-building. She has worked for artists spanning Bob Dylan to Justin Timberlake and is the co-creator of the Bloom Stage, an interdisciplinary arts performance stage, and the founder of art-centered wellness retreats that invite creativity, reflection, and care. description: Angeline, through the bliss of losing herself in creating a 10-second melody, and the inner peace of running freely on the playground before exams, discovers that true success is not about climbing the single "mountain" built on grades, rankings and others' approval. Instead, it is about hearing and following the true voice within her heart in the vast "sea" of her own, and exploring the thousands of possibilities in life at her own unique pace. Yiran Han, a 14-year-old outstanding eighth-grade student who loves both music and sports. She enjoys composing melodies with mobile apps and is active on the court—whether playing basketball, table tennis, badminton, or volleyball. To her, success is not about ranking, but about immersing herself in what she loves, mastering it step by step, and constantly pushing her limits. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: SUCCESS Not A Mountain, but An Open Field | Yiran Han | TEDxRDFIS Youth

Drawing on her own experience in a high-pressure educational environment — where she achieved external success such as straight A's, yet was trapped in exhaustion and emptiness from constant comparison with others — she analyzes the limitations of relying on extrinsic motivation. She then shares her transformation from "wanting to be someone else" to "truly loving volleyball", making it clear that intrinsic motivation (the passion itself) is the source of sustainable growth and real success. I’m Teodora, an 11th grade student at RDF International School. I moved to China almost two years ago, and I am currently experiencing an American-style education. Drawing on her own experience, she recounts how she broke free from the oppression of chasing grades and turned to the field of bioengineering that she is passionate about. Through launching projects such as the smart pet helmet, participating in and winning awards at international competitions, she has transformed her enthusiasm into tangible achievements and a unique application profile, ultimately earning recognition from top summer schools and prestigious academic opportunities. A diligent learner who never ceased her effort, Snow wishes to share her journey of success with others. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Dr. Cheryl Dublar, as an educator, offers a profound analysis of the widespread "involution" dilemma in modern education and life: a vicious cycle where people keep putting in more effort, yet end up trapped in a loop of minimal gains and overwhelming physical and mental exhaustion. On stage, she poses a gentle yet powerful question: When busyness itself becomes the goal, are we mistaking "fatigue" for "growth"? True education, she argues, should teach people to recognize and break free from this self-depleting cycle. I am an educator with more than fifteen years of experience teaching at both the high school and university levels. I hold a Doctor of Philosophy in Educational Management and have been teaching internationally since 2019. Despite my academic background and professional achievements, I experienced constant pressure to do more and achieve more. Over time, I observed the same pattern among my students—working harder while feeling increasingly 
exhausted rather than fulfill
title: ANTI-INVOLUTION | REDEFINE SUCCESS | Cheryl Dublar | TEDxRDFIS Youth

description: At four years old, Jeremy Qualls was engulfed in flames. As he left the hospital, his father told him to lead with fire. Decades later, through three unforgettable Post-it notes left on his pillow, Jeremy learned what that really meant. From a 5-21 coaching record to a school that reduced disciplinary referrals from 1,000 to 52, to a player who taught him more than he ever taught the player, Jeremy delivers a powerful reminder that true leadership is not about seeking power. It is about pointing the spotlight at the people you serve. Jeremy works with business leaders, school leaders, and community organizations to improve education, workforce development, and entry points into school systems for maximum ROI and collaboration. Jeremy has also developed workshops for training and keynote delivery around passions, "Leading with Fire", creating a positive work culture around his "Pirate Ship" mentality. description:
How can we build cities and mindsets that survive the earth's deepest tremors?

In this eye-opening TEDx talk, renowned Japanese Master Architect and Civil Engineer Yoshinori Moriwaki shares his profound insights into earthquake preparedness, bridging the seismic realities of Japan and Turkey. Having lived and worked in Turkey for over three decades, Moriwaki explains why earthquakes shouldn't be feared, but understood.

He breaks down the vital differences in structural engineering, disaster management, and cultural psychology between the two earthquake-prone nations. Through compelling personal stories and expert analysis, Moriwaki delivers a crucial message: it is not the earthquake that causes destruction, but unprepared buildings and lack of education. Discover practical steps we can take today to ensure a safer, more resilient tomorrow. Yoshinori Moriwaki, özellikle deprem riski yüksek bölgelerde güvenli şehirler oluşturma, sürdürülebilir kentleşme ve afet bilinci konularındaki

description: This speech begins with the classic scene from The Emperor's New Clothes, where a child speaks the truth. It argues that comedy is not just simple entertainment—it is a powerful tool that allows ordinary people to reveal the hidden truths of our time. Using examples like the black humor of World War II soldiers and jokes about shortages during the Soviet era, the speech shows how comedy wraps hard truths in laughter, becoming a safe way for people to express taboo topics and share collective emotions. The speech then deeply examines the three core forms of courage found in comedy: first, the courage to touch the collective pain of the era and create empathy; second, the courage to see beyond mainstream beliefs and amplify the voices of minority groups; and third, the courage to question authority by using humor to break down power and pretense, awakening people's critical thinking. The speech also makes a clear distinction between true comedy and cheap jokes that make fun of vulnerabl

description: This workshop uses Michelangelo's two classic works—David and The Dying Slave—as its central focus. By connecting these works to the historical context in which the artist created them, the workshop explores the deep theme of "external appearance versus inner essence." It offers an in-depth interpretation of the strong contrast between the visual surface of the two paintings and the human nature and spiritual power hidden beneath. It uncovers the core idea of "looking beyond the surface to find inner truth." The workshop then connects this artistic theme to today's society, pointing out that our world is full of anxiety, doubt, and restlessness. People are easily fooled by appearances, leading to blind comparison and emotional exhaustion. It fully demonstrates the real-life value of seeing through appearances and searching for the essence. description: This speech begins with the core idea that "sound and music can capture the emotions and precious moments of life that words and images often struggle to express." It first points out that music is not a language reserved only for professional creators—it is a living diary for ordinary people to record their lives. Then, by comparing the past barriers of music creation, such as limited resources and access to studios, the speech explains how today's technology has completely broken down those barriers—now a single laptop can serve as a complete recording studio. Next, using the speaker's own experience of writing an original song for their alma mater as an example, the speech shows how a simple humming idea after class eventually led to building the accompaniment, arranging the melody, writing the lyrics, and completing a final song. description:
Despite studying law, Nuri Turgut followed his passion for commerce and wrote a success story from the ground up. In his talk themed "Transformation: From Roots to Future," he explains how an initiative nurtured by local roots transformed into a global brand.

Turgut—the founder of the home textile brand Cottonbox, which currently exports to more than 60 countries, and the Chairman of the Board of the Denizli Industrialists and Businessmen Association (DESİAD)—shares the turning points on the path from contract manufacturing to creating his own brand, the risks taken on a journey started without capital, and the power of visionary design. Conveying the importance of value-added production and structural transformation through his own striking personal journey, this eye-opening talk guides all entrepreneurial spirits and the business world who want to push boundaries while embracing their roots. description: This speech begins with my own experience as a high school student living a high-pressure, "always online" life. I often find myself physically in the classroom but mentally somewhere else—a state of mind-body disconnection. This, the speech points out, is a health crisis that many people face today. It analyzes how sitting for too long leads to physical decline, and how long hours of screen time cause poor concentration and brain fog. It also shows how people try to escape pressure by being "busier and faster," only to trap their bodies in a vicious cycle of constant tension. The speech then breaks the stereotype that tai chi is just a slow exercise for the elderly. It explains how tai chi has evolved from a martial art for self-defense into a way to regulate the body and mind. It highlights the scientific benefits of tai chi: activating the parasympathetic nervous system, relieving chronic stress, and restoring the body's structural balance. In his talk themed "Transformation: From Roots to Future," Mustafa Fikret Uğur—Co-Founder and CEO of Magfi, who began his entrepreneurial journey at a very young age and passionately shapes technology—shares how he transformed the obstacles he faced into stepping stones for success.

description: This speech begins with a common scene in the subway—long lines waiting for the escalator while the stairs right next to it remain empty. It challenges the common belief that "humans are naturally lazy." First, drawing on the reality of job burnout in modern society and psychological research on decision fatigue, the speech explains that modern people are exhausted by work pressure and information overload. Choosing the escalator is not laziness but the brain's way of protecting its energy. Then, using the contrast of people paying money to work hard at the gym, the speech analyzes a modern dilemma: our effort is often externalized. Everyday hard work is ignored because it lacks recognition, measurement, and social proof, so people need external systems to discipline their self-control. At the same time, the speech points out that this phenomenon deeply reflects the characteristics of our time. description: This speech moves beyond people's visions of an AI future. Instead, it starts by looking back at the technological journey from the first computers to ChatGPT. It identifies a basic pattern of human tech innovation: "solving real-world problems — inventing new technologies — achieving the next level of progress." Through examples like how the Enigma machine led to the first computer, how the limits of vacuum tubes inspired the birth of the chip, and how the demand for 3D graphics drove NVIDIA to create its accelerators, the speech shows how technology builds on itself step by step, each invention enabling the next. It then explains the key roles of neural networks and the scaling law in AI development, showing that the birth of ChatGPT was the natural result of combining existing technologies. title: From "Lightbulbs" to ChatGPT | Yunzhe Qu | TEDxWLSA Shanghai Academy

description:
Dr. Shahna Mubarak explains that identity is not defined by appearance, achievements, or social labels, but by what we deeply believe about ourselves. She highlights that confidence is not just a trait, but biological—shaped by our thoughts and internal beliefs. When individuals feel heard and valued, their confidence naturally shifts, showing how mindset influences both behavior and outcomes.

She emphasizes that the brain focuses on what we believe to be true; negative beliefs reinforce insecurity, while positive beliefs open us to opportunities. Confidence, therefore, is something that can be learned and developed over time.

In a world full of labels and judgments, she reminds us that these perceptions do not define our true identity. Instead, individuals should focus on their strengths, growth, and inner energy. description: This speech begins with the striking contrast between the natural beauty of the Gannan grassland and the ecological damage caused by plastic pollution and overgrazing. It introduces the environmental meaning of “the echo of our time”—that every choice we make sends an echo through nature’s cycle. The speech outlines a clear environmental logic: short-sighted human development leads to ecological damage; nature strikes back through extreme weather and threats to wildlife; and finally, humans awaken and take action to restore the environment. Drawing on the UN Sustainable Development Goals, the speech shares local environmental protection practices from Gannan, such as a women’s cooperative turning plastic waste into woven products and the local government building solar-powered waste stations. It also talks about the speaker’s own actions, including organizing a SDG offline exhibition and setting up a campus SDG club. These examples show the dual power of collective efforts and individ

description: This speech begins with the national agricultural emergency in Colombia caused by the outbreak of Panama disease TR4 on banana farms. It first explains that commercial bananas are facing extinction due to monoculture farming, and that bananas—as the fourth largest food crop in the world—are directly linked to the livelihoods and diets of billions of people. The speech then looks back at the disappearance of the “Gros Michel” banana and how the “Cavendish” banana is now repeating the same fate. It also discusses how climate change is making the spread of diseases worse, revealing the deeper problem: global agricultural systems have sacrificed biodiversity for efficiency, and as a result, lost their long-term resilience. The speech further points out that monoculture supply chains are a common risk in many fields around the world. description: Jessica Rosado is a junior at Kihei Charter School and talks about her parent's immigration to the US with power and purpose. Everyday of her life, she has had challenges regarding her community, her identity, and her freedom. She has faced judgment, racism, and taunts whenever she discusses immigration. She always discusses her parent’s safety, and is worried about what the world is going to be like for them. Since the beginning of her high school life, she’s wondered how she can help the community and what she can do to speak up. Loving public speaking, Jessica knew that TEDx would be a step toward her plans for advocacy, public speaking, and community-involvement. During her presentation, she explains about immigration and how when purpose meets power, anything is possible. She expressed how power is in everyone, and her hope and determination towards the audience was to spread awareness and understand her point of view regarding immigrant rights. description: Talks about the power of cultural immersion and finding resilience in unfamiliar soil. After moving from the contained environment of Las Vegas to Hawaiʻi, Christian navigated the challenges of being an outsider by embracing local traditions rather than resisting them. Drawing from the metaphor of the ‘a‘ali‘i, a plant dismissed as a weed elsewhere but revered in Hawaiʻi for its ability to withstand fierce winds, he shares how learning ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi, practicing hula, and studying native ecosystems allowed him to grow deep, purposeful roots. By sharing his journey of self-replanting, Christian encourages others to step outside their comfort zones and engage with diverse worldviews to build a more unified global community. description: A volte la ribellione non si manifesta in un gesto di rottura ma in una forma di resistenza a quello che sembra l’inesorabile fluire delle cose. Rimanere fermi quando tutto ci spinge a correre, fare scelte di consumo consapevole, ridurre il nostro impatto sul mondo sono sfide che ci rendono migliori. E migliorano la qualità della vita, nostra e di chi ci circonda. Alessandro Lovisetto è un giovane imprenditore biellese con una forte passione per il digital e la sostenibilità. Ha creato Artknit Studios, una startup che connette le migliori manifatture tessili per rendere la maglieria di lusso più accessibile e più sostenibile, usando solo fibre naturali, certificate e una filiera corta e trasparente, secondo un nuovo modello di business, originale e fertile. Alessandro Lovisetto è un giovane imprenditore italiano con una forte passione per il digital e la sostenibilità. Dopo aver lavorato in giganti dell’alta tecnologia come Google e Rocket Internet, ha deciso di creare Artknit Studios
